To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecasts from major meteorological agencies converge on a Moscow high near 20°C for August 15, 2026, with ensemble model runs showing tight clustering between 19–21°C driven by variable cloud cover and weak synoptic pressure gradients that limit daytime solar heating. This atmospheric setup creates genuine uncertainty between the market’s leading 19°C (50.5%) and 20°C (42.5%) outcomes, as modest shifts in cloud timing or boundary-layer mixing could tip the daily maximum either way. Historical August averages near 20–22°C provide context, yet current conditions favor readings at or below the mean. Official measurements from Roshydromet will resolve the market, with final data releases expected later today.

Trader consensus, reflected in the 64.5% implied probability for 92-93°F and 94% combined odds for 90-95°F, aligns with model clusters around 91-92°F. Afternoon sea-breeze convergence or isolated convection could cap upside, and the next NWS forecast updates will refine resolution expectations before the day’s maximum is recorded.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and official guidance from the National Weather Service position a high near 100°F as the most likely outcome for Austin on August 15, 2026.** Persistent high pressure and dry air across South-Central Texas support daytime heating under mostly sunny skies, with latest point forecasts calling for a high of 100°F at Austin-Bergstrom International Airport—the station typically used for official readings. 

Climatologically, mid-August features average highs near 97°F, but the current pattern has sustained temperatures several degrees above normal for weeks, consistent with the market’s heavy weighting toward 100–101°F (57.5%). Nearby guidance shows a tight cluster between 100–102°F, with only modest upside risk if afternoon mixing or slight model shifts allow a brief push higher. Downside scenarios to the 98–99°F range remain possible if unexpected cloud cover or a weak boundary arrives, but current observations and short-range ensembles favor the 100–101°F bin as the consensus resolution.
